- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is rising, cap the forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to prevent false optimism.  
- After a forecast spike, if true outcome shows a sharp drop, adjust next forecast downward by 3–5% to reflect mean reversion.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true values by >3% over 3–5 days, apply a 2–3% downward bias to future forecasts.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.7), reduce forecast volatility by smoothing 3–5 day moving average to avoid overfitting sentiment noise.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is below 70% of forecast’s 10-day moving average, apply a 10–15% downward correction.
